name: Heron Lakes Golf Club
centre_source: box centre chosen from sourced points: clubhouse/range 45.6044,-122.7032 and 45.6018,-122.7027 (stymie map links), 45.6046,-122.7051 (golfn), Great Blue 45.6021,-122.6981 (OpenGolfAPI, from OSM); bracketed by PIR 45.5969,-122.6958 (Wikipedia), Force Lake 45.6047,-122.6936 (Wikipedia), Smith Lake (west) and the Columbia Slough (south). Not a surveyed centre; each course's extent is unknown until the OSM export
architects: Robert Trent Jones Jr. (Greenback with his father; Great Blue 1992; Top100 credits RTJ II associate Kyle Phillips)
renovations: 1987: third nine (Red) added; 1988 renamed Heron Lakes (was West Delta Park Golf Course)
1992: fourth nine; split into Greenback (original 18) and Great Blue (Red nine + new nine)
2025: new forward tees on Great Blue, bunker sand and restoration on both courses, re-rated by the OGA (Portland golf advisory committee minutes, Apr-Nov 2025)
2025: levee raise under study with the US Army Corps (nothing built)
access: public (City of Portland, Portland Parks & Recreation; managed by KemperSports)
notable: 2000 U.S. Amateur Public Links (Great Blue; D.J. Trahan)
PGA Northwest Open; NFL Quarterback Shootout
Golf Digest Top 75 Public (RTJ II portfolio, undated)
course records 64 Tiger Woods (Great Blue), 63 Johnny Miller (Greenback) (GolfPass 2010)
video_games: none found (searched EA/Tiger Woods PGA Tour, PGA Tour 2K, Links, Golden Tee)
water: six ponds dug at construction; Greenback six ponds (holes not listed); Great Blue 8 (pond guarding the fairway), 16 (lake and wetland along the fairway), 17 (slough), 18 (water right and in front of the green, lake behind); all red; Columbia Slough south of the site
